newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova raps Russian Duma for "interference".
newsitem.headline: Moldova raps Russian Duma for "interference".

text.p: Moldova said on Thursday that a call by Russia's Duma (lower house) to recognise Moldova's rebel Dnestr region as a zone of Russia's strategic interests was an unfriendly act and interference in its internal affairs.
"Such actions by the State Duma cannot be qualified otherwise than an interference in Moldova's internal affairs," a Moldovan foreign ministry statement said.

"This contravenes the principles and norms of international law," said the statement. "Using as a cover the thesis of protecting Russian citizens living abroad...the State Duma is in fact trying to provide support for separatism."
On Wednesday the Duma, which often takes hardline positions at odds with official government policy towards Russia's neighbours, passed the appeal to President Boris Yeltsin by a large majority.
It suggested that Russian troops should remain based in the Dnestr region, whose separatist government should get economic, military and cultural aid and support from Moscow.
The Russian troops, mostly recruited locally, are leftovers from the former Soviet 14th army, based on the left bank of the Dnestr river in what is now the separatist capital Tiraspol.

In 1994 Russia and Moldova signed an agreement to withdraw the remaining several thousand soldiers over a three-year period but the Russian Duma, where support for the breakaway Dnestr region is strong, never ratified it.
Alexander Papkin, Russian ambassador to Moldova, told Moldovan radio that the Duma's attitude to the Dnestr dispute had nothing to do with the official position of Russia's government.
"Russia's Foreign Ministry one more time reiterates its position that the Dnestr region is an inalienable part of an indivisible and territorially integral Moldova," Papkin said.
He noted that Russia, alongside Ukraine and the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe (OSCE), was mediating in Moldova's peace talks with the Dnestr leaders.
